newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope John Paul names new Chicago archbishop.
newsitem.headline: Pope John Paul names new Chicago archbishop.

text.p: Pope John Paul has appointed Archbishop Francis George to head Chicago's Roman Catholic church, the largest diocese in the United States, the Vatican said in a statement on Tuesday.
George will fill the post left vacant by Archbishop Joseph Bernardin, America's senior prelate, who died of cancer last year.
Bernardin, a member of the U.S. Catholic Church's liberal wing, had been Archbishop of Chicago since 1982 and was considered a possible successor to the Polish Pontiff.
George will move to Chicago from the diocese of Portland in Oregon, where he has been Archbishop for under a year.
The prelate was born in Chicago in 1937 and studied theology at the University of Ottawa in Canada. He became a Catholic priest in Chicago in Decmber 1963.
The Archbishop spent 12 years in Rome from the mid-1970s, graduating in theology from the Pontifical University of Urbaniana.
